housing.summary: Pisa is a mid-sized Tuscan university city; asking rents in the historic centre (Centro Storico) average roughly EUR 13 per square metre per month, so a small one-bedroom flat typically runs about EUR 500-700/month. The main online rental portals are Idealista (https://www.idealista.it/affitto-case/pisa/) and Immobiliare.it. Under Italian tenancy law (Law 392/1978) the security deposit is commonly capped at a maximum of three months' rent.

banking.summary: Newcomers open an account with a major retail bank; the largest networks present in Pisa are Intesa Sanpaolo, UniCredit and Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena (headquartered in nearby Siena, Tuscany). To open an account a foreigner needs a valid passport or national ID, an Italian codice fiscale (tax code) and proof of address; a resident account additionally requires a residence permit or work contract (source: https://yourwaytoitaly.it/en/articles/how-to-open-a-bank-account-in-italy-as-a-foreigner).
required_docs: Proof of address (residence permit or work contract for a resident account)
banks_named: Banca Monte dei Paschi di Siena

schools.summary: Pisa has no verified dedicated English-curriculum international school within the comune; families relocating with school-age children typically look to international options in the wider Tuscany region (e.g. Florence). No corridor-verified Pisa international school listing was available at time of harvest.

legal_admin.summary: On moving to Pisa a newcomer must register their residence (variazione di residenza / iscrizione anagrafica) with the Ufficio Anagrafe of the Comune di Pisa, within 20 days of the move. EU citizens register residence directly; non-EU nationals must first hold a valid permesso di soggiorno before registering. Authority: Comune di Pisa - Anagrafe.
legal_admin.registration_step: Register residence (variazione di residenza) at the Comune di Pisa Ufficio Anagrafe within 20 days of moving; EU citizens register directly, non-EU nationals must first obtain a permesso di soggiorno

tax_finance.summary: For individuals the Italian tax identifier is the Codice Fiscale, issued by the Agenzia delle Entrate. In Pisa it is handled by the Direzione Provinciale di Pisa (Galleria Giovan Battista Gerace 7, 56124 Pisa). The codice fiscale is required to open a bank account, sign a lease, register with the health service and be employed.

transport.summary: Regional and city bus services in Pisa are operated by Autolinee Toscane (brand 'at'; https://www.at-bus.it). A dedicated automated 'PisaMover' people-mover connects Pisa Centrale station to Pisa International Airport. A corridor-verified price for the Pisa urban monthly pass was not available at harvest. EU/EEA driving licences remain valid; non-EU residents must generally convert to an Italian licence within one year of establishing residence.
transport.driving_licence_exchange: EU/EEA licences remain valid; non-EU residents must generally convert to an Italian driving licence within one year of establishing residence (subject to reciprocity agreements)

healthcare.summary: Public healthcare is provided through the Servizio Sanitario Nazionale (SSN). New residents register with the local health authority (ASL) - for Pisa this is the Azienda USL Toscana Nord Ovest - to enrol in the SSN and obtain a tessera sanitaria (health card). Registration requires a codice fiscale, proof of residence and, for non-EU nationals, a valid permesso di soggiorno.
healthcare.registration: Register with the local ASL (Azienda USL Toscana Nord Ovest) to enrol in the SSN and obtain a tessera sanitaria; requires codice fiscale, proof of residence and (non-EU) a valid permesso di soggiorno
